when.quote: This document outlines the step-by-step workflow for agents to process CLI requests, including verification and final decision. These steps MUST be followed in the exact order listed.

starts.note: customer: start only when the account owner or an authorized account manager asks to raise the credit limit on a credit card. No document says the agent may offer an increase without being asked. If a request is denied and the customer asks again in the same conversation (for example after paying the balance down), that is a new customer request: run the resubmit steps.
starts.quote: Only the account owner or an authorized account manager may submit a CLI request for the account.

tools.not_used: The CLI job never orders a replacement card. The replacement tier document is cited only to map cards to tiers, and a pending replacement only blocks the CLI.
No CLI document names a tool for the customer to run. The agent submits, checks and decides the request itself.

The CLI job never moves money. If the customer asks to pay the balance down from checking after a high_utilization denial, that is the separate job paying_off_credit_card_balance_from_checking_account.
The CLI job reads no bank accounts. Only the separate payment job uses it to find the checking account.

steps.do: Check every criterion, in this order, using get_current_time for the dates. (1) Account age ≥ 120/90/60 days (Entry/Mid/Premium) from the open date. (2) Cooldown: no APPROVED prior request within 120/90/60 days; ignore the request just submitted and any denied ones. (3) No dispute with status open or under_review on this card. (4) No replacement order in a non-final state (pending or shipped). (5) No past-due balance. (6) Utilization = balance ÷ limit, strictly below 70%/80%/90%. (7) Consecutive on-time payments for the required months: 6 (Entry) or 3 (Mid/Premium). (8) Amount within the tier maximum.
steps.quote: You MUST check ALL of the following eligibility criteria before making an approval or denial decision as this ensures complete audit records.

steps.do: Unlock and call the approval with the new total limit (current limit + increase)

steps.do: Unlock and call the denial with the failing reason (e.g. 'pending_disputes' if there is an active dispute). If several criteria fail, use the first one in eval's check order. Codes: insufficient_account_age, cooldown_period_active, pending_disputes, pending_replacement_card, past_due_balance, high_utilization, insufficient_payment_history, requested_amount_exceeds_limit, other.
steps.if: any requirement is not met
steps.quote: Use the deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 tool to record the denial.

steps.do: Step 5: tell the customer the decision. For an approval, give the new total limit. For a denial, give the reason and say what must be resolved (lower utilization, finish a dispute or replacement, pay a past-due balance), and when they may reapply (for cooldown: the last approved request date plus 120/90/60 days). Do not expose internal tool details.
steps.quote: For approvals, confirm the new credit limit. For denials, explain the reason and when they may be eligible to reapply.

steps.do: For a high_utilization denial, explain that utilization (balance ÷ limit) must be below 70% (Entry), 80% (Mid) or 90% (Premium and above) when a request is submitted, that paying the balance down lowers it, and that a denied request starts no cooldown, so they may submit a new request as soon as utilization is below the threshold. If the customer asks to pay the balance from their Rho-Bank checking account, run paying_off_credit_card_balance_from_checking_account (its steps check funds and get authorization). Do not move money without that job.

jobs.done_when: The customer is verified and logged. Then one of these holds. (a) The CLI request was submitted within the tier maximum, every criterion was checked, exactly one of the approve or deny tools was called, and the customer was told the decision with its reason and reapply date, or the new limit. (b) The customer declined the tier-maximum amount and nothing was submitted. (c) A tool failed after a retry and a transfer was offered. (d) After a denial, the customer fixed the cause (for example paid the balance down through the payment job) and asked again, and a new request was submitted, checked in full and decided, and the customer was told the result.

open_questions: Step 3 of the CLI workflow doc ('Verify Payment History and Requested Amount') has no body. The payment history and amount rules come from doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_006.

The CLI rules list only entry, mid and premium tiers. Elite (Platinum) and Invitation (Diamond Elite) cards are treated as premium-tier-and-above, following the replacement documents. No CLI document states this directly.
No document names which tool shows a past-due balance. Use get_credit_card_accounts_by_user or get_payment_history_6183, whichever returns it.
When several criteria fail, the documents do not say which denial_reason to record. The workflow uses the first failing criterion in the documented order.

The documents do not say whether the request just submitted, or an earlier denied one, appears in get_credit_limit_increase_history_4829. Neither counts toward the cooldown, because only approved requests trigger it.

steps.do: Check ALL criteria before deciding. (1) Account age: days from the open date to now must be at least 120 (entry), 90 (mid) or 60 (premium), else 'insufficient_account_age'. (2) Cooldown: a previous APPROVED request (other than the one just submitted) less than 120/90/60 days ago gives 'cooldown_period_active'. Denied requests do not count. (3) Any dispute not closed or resolved gives 'pending_disputes'. (4) Any replacement order not delivered or cancelled gives 'pending_replacement_card'. (5) A past-due balance gives 'past_due_balance'. (6) Utilization (balance / credit limit) must be strictly below 70% (entry), 80% (mid) or 90% (premium), else 'high_utilization'. (7) The last 6 (entry) or 3 (mid/premium) months must all be on-time payments, else 'insufficient_payment_history'. (8) The amount must be within the tier maximum, else 'requested_amount_exceeds_limit'.
steps.quote: You MUST check ALL of the following eligibility criteria before making an approval or denial decision as this ensures complete audit records.

steps.do: Tell the customer the decision. If approved, confirm the new credit limit. If denied, explain the reason and when they can reapply: after the account-age date or cooldown end, once disputes are resolved or the replacement is delivered or cancelled, once the account is current, or once utilization is lowered below the threshold. Denied requests start no cooldown, so they may reapply as soon as the cause is fixed. If the customer then asks to pay down the balance from checking, run pay_credit_card_balance_from_checking, then start this job again at check_amount.
steps.quote: Inform the customer of the decision and provide next steps. For approvals, confirm the new credit limit. For denials, explain the reason and when they may be eligible to reapply.

steps.do: If a lookup returns an error or an ambiguous result, retry the call once. If it still fails, do not decide from partial data. Tell the customer the request cannot be completed now and offer a transfer to a human agent, calling transfer_to_human_agents only if they accept.
